summary:
Project Name: OrbitWell
Team Name: Astronaut Mission
Challenge: Health Monitoring Software Developing
What did you develop?
I developed OrbitWell, an intelligent, web-based telemetry dashboard designed to monitor and optimize astronaut health and cognitive performance in real-time. The platform features an intuitive UI divided into core modules: a Central Dashboard, Systems & Vitals (tracking SpO2, fluid/hydration, and body temperature), Reflex and Coordination testing, and an Alert & NASA Data integration system.  
How does it address the challenge?
OrbitWell addresses the Health Monitoring Software challenge by providing an autonomous local hub that tracks critical physiological and neurological parameters continuously, bypassing communication delays with Earth.
Why is it important?
During deep-space missions, astronauts face extreme isolation and microgravity risks. OrbitWell ensures crew safety by detecting anomalies instantly, preventing minor health shifts from becoming emergencies, and empowering astronauts to stay healthy millions of miles from Earth.
details: What It Does & How It Works OrbitWell (developed by team Astronaut Mission for the Health Monitoring Software Developing challenge) is a real-time, web-based astronaut health and cognitive telemetry hub. It acts as an onboard medical co-pilot that continuously tracks, analyzes, and visualizes crew vitals and neurological readiness during long-duration space missions. The platform is organized into five core modules: Dashboard / Hub: Displays an instant mission status overview mission duration timer, and an ⁠All Systems Nominal⁠ indicator Systems & Vitals: Monitors critical physiological telemetry in real time, including Oxygen Level (⁠SpO2: 98.4%⁠), Fluid/Hydration status (⁠85.0% - Safe⁠), and Core Body Temperature (⁠36.8 °C⁠).  Reflex Test: Evaluates neurological response times (⁠Reflex Average⁠) to detect early signs of cognitive fatigue.  Coordination Module: Measures hand-eye coordination and fine motor skills required for complex spacecraft operations. Alert & NASA Data: Integrates live simulated NASA telemetry streams and triggers automated safety alerts whenever vital signs deviate from safe thresholds. Benefits & Intended Impact Deep-space missions introduce significant communication delays with Earth, making real-time ground control medical intervention impossible during emergencies. OrbitWell solves this by giving astronauts complete local autonomy over their health monitoring. By catching subtle physiological or cognitive shifts early—such as dehydration, oxygen drops, or slowed reflexes—it prevents minor anomalies from escalating into critical medical emergencies. Beyond space exploration, its lightweight architecture can be adapted for extreme, isolated environments on Earth, such as polar research stations, submarines, and disaster response teams. Tools, Technologies & Hardware Used Frontend & Core Development: Built using modern, lightweight web technologies (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript) to ensure fast rendering, zero lag, and seamless cross-device compatibility. UI/UX Design & Prototyping: Designed with a minimalist, high-contrast dark mode interface, with presentation assets and documentation created via powerpoint and Google Workspace. Hardware Optimization: Engineered and tested to run smoothly even on resource-constrained, older hardware, proving its reliability on low-power spacecraft display terminals. Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered Holistic Health Approach: Instead of only tracking physical vitals like heart rate or oxygen, we creatively combined physiological telemetry with interactive Reflex and Coordination mini-assessments, recognizing that mental sharpness and motor control are just as critical as physical health in microgravity. Human-Centered Spacecraft Ergonomics:our team prioritized cognitive load reduction and visual ergonomics. We chose a high-contrast dark UI specifically tailored for low-light spacecraft cabins, ensuring astronauts can read critical metrics at a glance without eye strain or information overload.
